items.title: 53571_Mary Lou Williams oral history interview
items.q: Moe Ash heard Erroll Garner and he said, 'Mary, try to get Errd1 Garner and Art Tatum to record.' ... I said, 'I think it will cost you about $1500 for Art Tatum; $750 for Errd1.' He said, 'I don't care; I'll pay them. Get them.'

ctx.x: Cafe Society uptown. He had both Cafe Society uptown, Barney Josephson did, and Cafe Society downtown. So I began hanging out on 52nd Street with the cats and they knew that I always helped musicians and so they'd - we'd come uptown around 4 o'clock or 4:30 in the morning and stay up all day, playing. There was Tadd Dameron, Bud Powell, Erroll Garner, Mel (Torme D'Armaine), and Miles Davis. Let's see, another trumpet player - Fats Navarro. A tenor man that was with Benny Goodman when he came out East - Wardell…
Oh, you played at your place, you mean?

items.title: 53571_Mary Lou Williams oral history interview
items.q: Moe Ash heard Erroll Garner and he said, 'Mary, try to get Errd1 Garner and Art Tatum to record.' ... I said, 'I think it will cost you about $1500 for Art Tatum; $750 for Errd1.'

ctx.x: on a vacation. By the way, we're both from Pittsburgh. He had been to New York and was a little discouraged. I said, "Come on back." So he came back later on, his girl friend or someone brought him here. Moe Ash heard Erroll Garner and he said, "Mary, try to get Errd1 Garner and Art Tatum to record." I knew Errd1 Garner needed money. I said, "I think it will cost you about $1500 for Art Tatum; $750 for Errd1." He said, "I don't care; I'll pay them. Get them." Moe Ash was so great that when I talked with Art…
But after you made the records for Moe did they get out much? Was there much circulation?
